question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed opt-in readiness v1 contract, including `gateway.readiness` activation, required/advisory aggregation, subject identity, and activation-scoped plugin providers?
rationale: These choices define new configuration and plugin-facing compatibility commitments; documentation edits alone cannot establish the intended long-term contract.

options.title: Accept narrow opt-in v1
options.body: Approve the explicit activation boundary and bounded provider contract, while keeping legacy readiness behavior authoritative when readiness is unconfigured.

options.title: Narrow the public contract
options.body: Approve only core canonical conditions now and defer plugin provider registration or subject reconciliation until their owners provide a smaller follow-up RFC.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Pause the RFC until the linked runtime implementation demonstrates a maintainer-approved compatibility and rollout path.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow opt-in v1
recommendation.body: Approve the explicit activation boundary and bounded provider contract, while keeping legacy readiness behavior authoritative when readiness is unconfigured.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing contact because they maintain this RFC and coordinate the linked implementation stack; the final decision remains a repository maintainer choice.
